correctness.rationale: Every perimeter-halving pair spans two distinct triangle sides, and for the shared vertex V the half-perimeter arc yields u+v=s. The cosine law gives |pq|²=s²sin²(θ_V/2)+(u−v)²cos²(θ_V/2), minimized only at u=v=s/2 and a smallest-angle vertex. Feasibility follows because both incident sides exceed s/2. Ordered tangent lengths x≥y≥z>0 and Heron/half-angle identities give A/h²=((x+y)(x+z)/s²)√(sx/(yz))≥(4/9)√3, with equality only x=y=z. Finite rational and direct minimization checks support, not replace, this proof.

scientific_scope: All nondegenerate planar Euclidean triangles only. Area-halving chords and general convex cycles are excluded.

value.rationale: The area relative to squared minimum perimeter-halving chord is a recognized convex-geometry extremal quantity. The equilateral benchmark and weaker general bound motivate an exact all-triangle sharp result. The theorem adds a global inequality, rigidity of equilateral equality, and an exhaustive constructive classification of minimizing chords, without claiming the open general convex-cycle case.
